issues.legal_issue: An unexhausted statutory appeal does not justify summarily dismissing a constitutional writ challenge where the petitioner challenges the authority or legal basis for the proceedings as ultra vires or alleges a violation of natural justice.
material_facts: The taxing officer assessed the appellant for one tax year under legislation whose continued validity and the authority of the assessing body the appellant challenged.
The appellant also challenged the constitutionality of the taxing provisions.
For a later tax year, the taxing officer made assessments without giving notice or inviting objections, and the appellant alleged that the assessment procedure violated natural justice.
The High Court dismissed the writ petition solely because the appellant had not pursued a statutory appeal.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in summarily dismissing the writ petition on the ground that a statutory appeal had not been exhausted. Its dismissal was set aside and the writ petition was restored for consideration in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: The existence of an adequate statutory remedy is relevant to the discretionary exercise of jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution, but exhaustion is a rule of policy and discretion, not a rule of law. Recognized exceptions include proceedings taken under an ultra vires provision and an impugned order made in violation of natural justice. The Court relied on Rashid Ahmed v. The Municipal Board, Kairana; State of Uttar Pradesh v. Mohammad Nooh; Carl Still G.m.b.H. v. State of Bihar; and The Bengal Immunity Co. Ltd. v. State of Bihar.

rule.if: constitutional_writ_challenge and alternative_statutory_remedy_unexhausted and (ultra_vires_challenge or natural_justice_violation_alleged)

predicates.constitutional_writ_challenge: The aggrieved person brought a constitutional writ challenge to the impugned proceedings or order.
predicates.alternative_statutory_remedy_unexhausted: The aggrieved person had not pursued an available statutory remedy before seeking the writ.
predicates.ultra_vires_challenge: The aggrieved person challenged the legal authority for the proceedings or the validity of the legal basis on which they were taken.
predicates.natural_justice_violation_alleged: The aggrieved person alleged that the impugned order was made without the notice, opportunity to object, or hearing required for a fair procedure.

issues.definition: When an unexhausted statutory remedy exists, a court may not summarily dismiss a constitutional writ challenge for nonexhaustion if the person challenges the proceedings as unauthorized or alleges that the order was made without fair procedure.
